title: 2.1.40 Print Settings Advisor
description: Given filament type and layer height, print a recommended print temperature using else if and logical operators. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: practice for else if chains (book 2.1.4) and combining conditions (book 2.1.8); scenario named in curriculum-plan §2.1 In-Class Activities: 'print settings advisor'

steps.title: Declare filament and layer height
steps.instructions: Create a variable called filamentType set to 'PLA', 'PETG', or 'ABS', and a variable called layerHeight set to a number of millimeters (e.g. 0.2).

steps.title: Chain the recommendation
steps.instructions: Write an else if chain that checks filamentType and recommends a print temperature: 'PLA' -> 200, 'PETG' -> 235, 'ABS' -> 250, anything else -> log 'Unknown filament type'. Log the recommended temperature.

steps.title: Add a layer-height warning
steps.instructions: Add a separate if statement that uses && or || to warn when layerHeight is outside a safe range (for example, less than 0.1 or greater than 0.4). Log a warning message when that's true.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[set filamentType and layerHeight]
  B --> C{a known filament}
  C -- yes --> D[/log its temperature/]
  C -- no --> E[/log Unknown filament type/]
  E --> F{layer height outside the safe range}
  D --> F
  F -- yes --> G[/log a warning/]
  F -- no --> H([End])
  G --> H

requirements.title: PLA branch logs 200
requirements.description: if condition checks filamentType === 'PLA' and logs 200

requirements.description: an else if condition checks filamentType === 'PETG' and logs 235

requirements.title: ABS branch chains and logs 250
requirements.description: an else if condition checks filamentType === 'ABS' and logs 250

requirements.title: final else logs Unknown filament type
requirements.description: the closing else branch logs a message containing 'Unknown filament type'

requirements.title: separate if warns on layerHeight range
requirements.description: a separate if condition compares layerHeight on both sides of && or ||

Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
